messages:
rachel: Heads-up — CS asked if we can do temporary burst overrides for AcmeCorp during a big demo next week. Need a quick plan for UI + API + safety. Thoughts?

devin: We already have an internal override API but it's admin-only. Example payload: ```POST /internal/quotas/override {"org_id":"acme","delta_tokens":500000,"expires_at":"2024-12-01T10:00:00Z","reason":"demo"}``` Needs auth + audit.

sam: API shape is fine. Risk: if we allow arbitrary delta_tokens without caps customers or CS could bypass quotas. We should enforce a max multiplier (e.g. 3x baseline) and require approver metadata.

maya: For Console UX: show an active override banner on org page, who created it, expiration, and a big "Revoke" button. Also add a timeline entry and highlight usage that consumed override tokens in billing views.

sophie: CS perspective — we want a request workflow, not a direct toggle. CS files request -> attaches to ticket -> 2-person approval (ops + security). Also include templated justification.

leo: Product think: prefer a safe "soft override" first: visible to metrics and billing but does not change hard throttles until a second approval. Less blast radius.

devin: Ops: implement per-org "burst window" telemetry: track burst consumption vs baseline, % used in first 10m, and alert when >80% of granted credits used immediately.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: quota-service v3.4 rollout -> staging started (sha=abc123).

sam: Telemetry fields we need: override_id, approver_id, request_source (CS/manual/API), delta_tokens, cap_multiplier, and a boolean forced_revoke. Add them to the logging schema.

rachel: Edge case: our runtime uses leaky-bucket style refill (rate r). If we just add delta_tokens we can create a very long tail where customers keep pumping requests after demo. Suggest separate "burst credits" ledger consumed before normal bucket refill.

devin: Implementation sketch: (1) burst credits ledger per org consumed first, (2) normal bucket continues refill as before, (3) cap multiplier enforcement, (4) audit events for every grant/consume/revoke, (5) API + console hooks.

maya: Telemetry/UI metric: surface "burst efficiency" = tokens_consumed / extra_tokens_granted in console and daily report. Helps detect waste.

sophie: Can we auto-revoke if anomaly detection flags abuse? CS wants an automatic safety net to protect SLOs.

sam: We can add a safety-kill: if request rate > X tokens/s and error rate spikes or queue lengths increase, auto-revoke and create a high-priority incident. Need tuning to avoid false positives during legitimate spikes.

leo: Rollout plan: behind feature flag per-org, internal beta for Redwood orgs, then 3 pilot customers with CS runbooks, collect 2 weeks of telemetry, then gradual enable.

rachel: I'll write an RFC with diagrams. Action items: @devin - API + caps; @sam - telemetry schema + safety kill thresholds; @maya - console mockups + request flow; @sophie - CS request/approve flow; @leo - rollout plan and pilot signups. Ping here if blocked. :thumbsup:
